items.title: How Long Do Wealth Shocks Persist? Less Than Three Generations in England, 1700–2026
items.excerpt: What happens across generations to wealth shocks? Do they endure and even magnify, or do they dissipate? By implication, how much modern wealth is attributable to events before 1900? This paper uses random shocks to family size in England before 1880 that created wealth shocks for the children to measure the persistence of wealth shocks.

explained.headline: Ebola Spreads to Kenya and Nigeria Amid Airport Inquiries

happened.text: Kenya has recorded its second death from Ebola as it handles its first ever outbreak of the disease.
A 65-year-old woman who was a close family member of the first victim died after being placed in quarantine, according to the health ministry.
Nigeria has confirmed its single imported case of Ebola involving a woman in the capital Abuja, prompting intensive contact tracing.

background.text: The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention is an organisation that provides public health services and coordination across the continent.
African health officials noted that the first confirmed patients in Kenya and Nigeria both passed through Uganda's Entebbe International Airport on October 3.

matters.text: Melaku Yirga, vice-president for Africa at Prosper Global, stated that the confirmation of Ebola in Kenya and Nigeria reinforces the need for countries to work closely together to prevent further transmission.
Yirga stated that what matters most now is speed, sharing information across borders without delay and ensuring frontline health workers and local organisations have the resources to respond quickly.
The outbreak threatens to strain healthcare systems and heighten economic worries for residents in affected nations.

uncertain.text: Health officials are investigating whether the patient in Nigeria may have come into contact with the Kenyan patient at the Ugandan airport.
Switzerland disputed accounts that the Nigerian patient had visited the Democratic Republic of Congo, leaving her exact source of exposure unclear.
Kenyan health authorities are also searching for an untraced Ugandan national identified as a contact of the deceased first patient.

terms.definition: A rare and severe viral disease that causes fever, severe bleeding, and organ impairment.
The process of identifying, assessing, and managing people who have been exposed to an infected individual to prevent further transmission.

removed.text: The current outbreak began in the Democratic Republic of Congo in May and has become the most geographically widespread in history.
why: The evidence does not describe this as the most geographically widespread outbreak in history.

explained.headline: Israel launches Hebron demolitions and siege after soldiers killed

happened.text: The Israeli military has begun demolishing Palestinian buildings in Hebron after two gunmen killed two Israeli soldiers and injured three others near a checkpoint outside the city.

background.text: Separately, displaced West Bank Palestinians face growing hunger following a 50 percent reduction in food aid recipients by the United Nations World Food Programme due to funding constraints.

matters.text: Lawyers and human rights advocates argue that the home demolitions violate international law regarding collective punishment.
Ubai Aboudi, an economist and human rights activist, stated that the West Bank is facing a severe humanitarian and financial crisis.

uncertain.text: The World Food Programme noted that aid could potentially be reinstated for some beneficiaries in the future, with notices sent via text message.

terms.definition: A food-assistance branch of the United Nations providing aid worldwide.
The interim administrative body governing parts of the West Bank.

removed.text: The events follow a surge of settlement expansion and violence in the occupied West Bank since October 2023.
Benjamin Netanyahu announced a siege on Hebron and neighbouring Halhul, promising mass demolitions and forced displacement.
why: The claim states the siege and displacement as facts rather than reporting them as Netanyahu's stated intentions.

removed.text: Bezalel Smotrich, the far-right finance minister, shared a video of himself in front of a bulldozer tearing down a Palestinian home without permits to create deterrence.
why: The evidence does not mention the absence of permits as the motivation for the demolition.

removed.text: Israel's far-right coalition government faces general elections, with polls indicating it may lose its majority.
why: The claim incorrectly states the loss of majority as fact rather than a likely possibility.

removed.text: Israel Katz, the defence minister, stated that Hebron would face the same destruction and forced displacement seen in Gaza, Lebanon, and the Jenin refugee camp.
why: The evidence mentions comparison to Jenin, but does not state Katz cited Lebanon as a comparison.

removed.text: Benjamin Netanyahu stated that plans for the largest military operation in the West Bank since 1967 have been drawn up, though no specific date has been set.
why: The claim ignores the 'about' qualifier regarding the displacement figures from 1967.

explained.headline: Fire at Adolf Hitler's Eagle's Nest mountain retreat

happened.text: Police in Bavaria detained a suspect during a fire at Adolf Hitler's former mountain retreat, known as the Eagle's Nest.
About 200 emergency personnel were deployed to tackle the blaze at the remote residence, though difficult terrain hindered their efforts.
Authorities reported that nobody was injured in the incident.

background.text: The building, formally called the Kehlsteinhaus, was completed by the Nazis in 1938 and served as a part-time seat of government.
The retreat survived destruction after the defeat of the Nazi regime in 1945 and later became a popular tourist destination housing a mountain inn.

matters.text: German media reported that investigators suspected the fire was the result of arson.

uncertain.text: Police stated that a criminal investigation is under way to determine whether the detained suspect is connected to the fire.

problems: The text incorrectly identifies the Eagle's Nest as the site of the fire, when it occurred elsewhere.

explained.headline: US Justice Department Sues Over Alaska Senate Candidates

happened.text: The United States Department of Justice filed a federal lawsuit in Alaska seeking to prevent the state from certifying its Senate election results if Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan narrowly loses.

The department argued in court filings that the presence of a second candidate named Dan Sullivan on the ballot is deliberately designed to confuse voters and mislead them into casting ballots for the wrong person.
United States President Donald Trump acknowledged that he directed the department to take this legal action.

background.text: Senator Dan Sullivan is running for his third six-year term in the Senate against Mary Peltola, a former congresswoman and the first Alaska Native elected to the United States House of Representatives.
The second candidate on the ballot, Daniel J Sullivan Jr, is a retired elementary schoolteacher and former United States Forest Service employee who registered as a Republican this year.
Although Alaska election officials initially disqualified the second candidate, the Alaska Supreme Court subsequently ruled that both men may remain on the ballot.

matters.text: Forrest Nabors stated that the similar names could swing the election if voters intending to re-elect the senator accidentally vote for his namesake.
Nabors also noted that the lawsuit will at least raise awareness of the issue among voters, which may reduce the number of mistaken votes.
The outcome of the race could influence which political party controls the United States Senate.

uncertain.text: Experts disagree on whether voter confusion will actually occur or how officials could accurately measure voter intent.
Legal scholars have questioned the validity of the Justice Department's legal arguments, with one describing the likelihood of the lawsuit's success as extremely low.
It remains unverified whether any federal court will order Alaska to suspend its certification process.

terms.definition: An electoral system where voters rank candidates in order of preference rather than choosing just one.

problems: The text refers to the senator running for a third term, but he is currently in his first term.
The explanation fails to mention the senator's actual political party, despite mentioning the other candidate's party affiliation.
